Description: The J.D./Master of Science in Finance joint-degree program is designed for students who wish to focus on securities and commodities law for a law firm, brokerage firm, commodity exchange, or trading company. [3] Students gain a unique perspective on the economics of financial products and markets that are used to advise clients, to propose regulation, or to litigate. [3] Enrollment in the J.D./Master of Science in Finance joint-degree program enables a student to obtain a J.D. degree from Chicago-Kent and an M.S. degree from Illinois Tech's Stuart School of Business in approximately three and a half to four years of full-time study or five to six years of part-time study. [3]
Accredidation: Illinois Institute of Technology is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [8] Chicago-Kent College of Law is accredited by the American Bar Association. [8]

ProgramName: J.D./Master of Public Health (joint degree in cooperation with University of Illinois at Chicago)
Requirements: Application for admission to the JD/MPH program must be made separately to the JD program and the MPH program. Applicants must file a Declaration of Intent to Pursue a Combined Degree form with both colleges prior to starting their first semester in the MPH program. Applicants must possess the minimum of a US baccalaureate degree to be considered for admission. [1]
MinimumGreScore: 292 (quantitative + verbal) and 2.5 (analytical writing) for professional master's and master of science applicants; 298 (quantitative + verbal) and 3.0 (analytical writing) for doctoral applicants
ScholarshipAmount: Full-tuition scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: The program normally requires a bachelor's degree in mathematics or applied mathematics. [2] Candidates whose degree is in another field (for example, computer science, physics, or engineering) and whose background in mathematics is strong are also eligible for admission and are encouraged to apply. [2] Applicants should have a bachelor's degree from an accredited university. [2] A cumulative GPA of 3.5/4.0 is usually required. [2] The applicants must also have demonstrated the potential for conducting original research in applied mathematics. [2] TOEFL scores (if required) should be a minimum of 80/550 (internet-based/paper-based test scores). [2] Three letters of recommendation are required. [2, 3] GRE scores are optional, and typically, admitted students score at least 165 on the quantitative portion of the GRE; however, meeting the minimum or typical GPA and test score requirements does not guarantee admission. [2, 3]
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Mathematics program provides advanced education through advanced coursework, independent study, and original, creative research to make a significant contribution to the field of applied mathematics and to prepare students for careers in academia and industrial research. [26]
MinimumGreScore: typically, admitted students score at least 165 on the quantitative portion of the GRE
ScholarshipAmount: Teaching or research assistantships that cover tuition and provide a competitive monthly stipend are offered.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture
Requirements: An applicant to the doctoral program generally must hold a professional Master of Architecture degree (M.Arch.), or Master of Science in Architecture (M.S.Arch.) from a NAAB-accredited U.S. university or Master of Landscape Architecture (M.L.A.) from an LAAB-accredited U.S. university or the equivalent. Students with graduate degrees in allied fields, such as engineering and art history, are also eligible. The applicant should meet all entrance requirements of the university's Graduate College, plus a minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale. [23] Required application materials include an online application, official transcripts, Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores, three letters of recommendation, a portfolio, and a statement of purpose. [35]
Concentration: ['Technologies of the Built Environment (TBE)', 'History, Theory, and Criticism (HTC)']
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Architecture program is for those individuals who desire to pursue careers in academia and/or in research-based professional practice. As the most advanced academic degree, the Ph.D. recognizes both the highest level of expertise and the production of significant novel work. The program, which is offered in two tracks, Technologies of the Built Environment (TBE) and History, Theory, and Criticism (HTC), demands a deep understanding of the related theories in contemporary intellectual terrain, a command yolks of a commitment to advanced research methodologies, and a commitment to critical inquiry that extends the frontiers of knowledge. The program begins with advanced coursework and culminates in a dissertation that is the result of extensive, original, and rigorous research and thought. The Ph.D. program grows out of the school's collective commitment to progressive research that is grounded in the realities of the workplace and devoted to contesting existing values and ideologies. Doctoral students also have the opportunity to participate in the experiments of design studios and later help guide these efforts in mentoring roles, helping to shape the debate within the college through their involvement in the college's “advanced studio.” [6]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Architectural Engineering
Requirements: The Doctor of Philosophy in Architectural Engineering program requires a minimum of 72 credit hours beyond the bachelor's degree, including the master's degree studies. [4] Applicants are expected to have already obtained both a B.S. and M.S. degree in architectural engineering or a closely related engineering discipline such as civil engineering, environmental engineering, mechanical engineering, and others. [4] Candidates must pass written qualifying and comprehensive examinations and must defend their thesis in an oral exam. [4] For admission, a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0/4.0 is required. [3] The minimum GRE scores are 292 (quantitative + verbal) and 2.5 (analytical writing). [3]
Concentration: ['Building energy and environmental systems', 'Structures', 'Construction engineering and management']
Description: Illinois Tech's Doctor of Philosophy in Architectural Engineering degree is awarded in recognition of a high level of mastery in the field of architectural engineering and upon demonstration of a distinct ability to make substantial creative contributions to knowledge in the field. The doctoral recipient will be capable of continuing efforts toward advancement of knowledge and achievement in research while pursuing an academic or industrial career. [4] The objective of the program is to provide an avenue for the advanced study of the design, construction, and operation of buildings and their systems. [5] This degree is recommended for those who expect to engage in a professional career in research, teaching, or technical work of an advanced nature focused on the design, construction, and operation of buildings and their systems. [4] Through state-of-the-art and original research, students are expected to achieve a high level of mastery in the study of buildings and their systems, which should be demonstrated by successful defense of their dissertation and the publication of novel research results in peer-reviewed academic journals. [5]
MaxFails: The official university website does not specify a maximum number of failing grades. However, it states that a cumulative GPA below 3.0 will result in academic probation, and failure to raise the GPA can lead to dismissal. [99] Courses with a grade of 'C' or lower do not count towards the degree and may only be repeated once.
ScholarshipAmount: The ACE Award, a partial-tuition scholarship for master's level study at Armour College of Engineering, covers the cost of three credit hours per semester for up to two semesters. [88] Other scholarships may also be available.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships such as the ACE Award are available. [88] The Armour College Scholarship Fund also provides support for economically disadvantaged students. [80]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biology
Requirements: General university-level application requirements are not specified. Application requirements are program-specific. Prospective students should refer to the individual program pages for detailed requirements.
Department: Lewis College of Science and Letters
Concentration: ['Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology (EEO)', 'Cell, Molecular, Health, and Disease Biology (CMHD)']
Description: The PhD in Biology offers students two distinct degree tracks that allow students to obtain broad, foundational training in modern biology while also affording a focused, specialized research experience: (1) Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology (EEO) and (2) Cell, Molecular, Health, and Disease Biology (CMHD). [3] The program is grounded in coursework involving current biological concepts and culminates in the defense of a dissertation describing novel and quality research conducted independently by the student. [3] PhD graduates in Biology are highly competitive for positions in academic settings, industry, and international research facilities. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree* conferred with a minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0/4.0 (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution for regular admission. [6] There are no specific courses that are required for the doctoral degree in biomedical engineering. However, a minimum of three courses in life science, three courses in mathematics, and six courses in biomedical engineering or other engineering-related courses are required. [8]
Description: This degree is awarded in recognition of a high level of mastery in subject matter and a significant original research contribution in biomedical engineering. The Ph.D. recipient will be capable of a continuing effort toward the advancement of knowledge and achievement in research and other scholarly activities and may pursue a career in a medical, industrial, or academic environment. [14]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: For regular admission, Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or its equivalent. [43] The general application materials for a degree-seeking student include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, a professional statement, required test scores, letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV. [47] Specifically for Ph.D. programs, two letters of recommendation are required. [44] For this specific program, the Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering, students must also pass a written qualifying examination within three semesters of admission which covers thermodynamics, reaction engineering and kinetics, transport phenomena, and process modeling and control. [14]
Description: Illinois Tech's Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering is awarded to students in recognition of mastery in chemical/biological engineering and upon demonstration of an ability to make substantial creative contributions to the advancement of chemical engineering. The recipients of these degrees will be capable of continuing efforts toward the advancement of knowledge and achievement in research while pursuing an academic or industrial research career.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: A minimum of 72 credit hours is required for the Ph.D. in Chemistry. Students who have received an M.S. degree from another university may petition for transfer of up to 32 credit hours, applicable toward the Ph.D. degree. Students must pass the Ph.D. qualifying examination by the end of their fourth semester in the program. To pass the comprehensive examination, students need to write a research progress report and proposal and defend it before a faculty committee. Students must pass the comprehensive exam at least a year prior to their thesis defense. The final phase in the Ph.D. degree program is the successful oral defense of the dissertation and submission of a Ph.D. dissertation approved by the academic adviser and the thesis committee. [29]
Description: Illinois Tech's chemistry program spans the traditional areas of research in physical, polymer, organic, inorganic, analytical, and biological chemistry. Prepare for a career in academia, industry, or government. A minimum of 72 credit hours is required for the Ph.D. in Chemistry. Students who have received an M.S. degree from another university may petition for transfer of up to 32 credit hours, applicable toward the Ph.D. degree. Students must pass the Ph.D. qualifying examination by the end of their fourth semester in the program. To pass the comprehensive examination, students need to write a research progress report and proposal and defend it before a faculty committee. The final phase in the Ph.D. degree program is the successful oral defense of the dissertation and submission of a Ph.D. dissertation approved by the academic adviser and the thesis committee.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil Engineering
Requirements: Admission to this program requires an MS in Civil Engineering or equivalent with a GPA of 3.5 or better (on a 0-4 scale). [52] Foreign applicants must take the TOEFL examination and submit the results for consideration. [52]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Clinical Psychology
Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Engineering
Requirements: Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree conferred with a minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0/4.0 (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution for regular admission. [100] For the Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Engineering, applicants must have a graduate (MS) grade point average (GPA) of 3.6 or above, or students with an undergraduate GPA of 3.5 or above may apply for direct admission. [1] All applicants must submit Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. [1] Two letters of recommendation are required for Ph.D. programs. [98] All students who have their degrees from a country where English is not the native language must provide the TOEFL examination results. [1]
Department: Armour College of Engineering, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Fees.1: The estimated tuition for the 2025–2026 academic year is $33,318, based on 18 credit hours per year. [77]
Description: The Ph.D. program in computer engineering in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering is aimed at preparing its graduates to become leaders in research and development in industry, academia, as well as government organizations. [1] Under guidance of faculty members, Ph.D. students do research in areas such as computer systems, computer networks, and artificial intelligence. [1] Students work in research labs in ECE Department equipped with state-of-the-art computing systems, develop and implement new concepts in hardware and software components of advanced computer-based systems. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science
Requirements: The minimum standards for admission to the computer science Ph.D. program are: Master's program, certificate, and non-degree applicants with bachelor's degrees outside of computer science may be required to complete one or more of the following courses. Mastery of the material they cover is considered necessary for graduate-level study and is required for completion of a degree program or certificate. In addition, applicants who have not had at least one course in calculus will be required to take one. Grades of “B” or better are required in all these courses. Credit hours from them cannot be applied toward a degree or certificate. [3] Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree* that is conferred with a minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution for regular admission. [4] Three letters of recommendation are required by the Department of Computer Science. [3] A personal statement. [3] Good academic standing is required for applicants who are currently pursuing a graduate degree at another university or in another department at Illinois Tech. [3] For applicants with degrees from schools where the primary language of instruction was not English, a minimum score of 70 on the internet-based TOEFL, 47 on the PTE, or 5.5 on the IELTS exam is required for admission consideration. [3]
Department: College of Computing, Department of Computer Science
Concentration: ['Theory of computation', 'Systems', 'Programming languages', 'Networks and security', 'Databases', 'Software engineering', 'Computational intelligence']
Description: The doctoral program is designed for those students who have an interest in pursuing an academic or industrial research career. To be awarded a Ph.D. a student must demonstrate mastery in several areas of computer science and must make a significant original contribution to research in the field of computer science. On entry into the program, a student is required to take coursework in a number of areas and pass written and oral qualifying exams. Next, the student must formulate a thesis research problem and present it and the proposed research to a committee of faculty at a comprehensive exam. [8]
MinimumGreScore: 304 (quantitative + verbal), 3.5 (analytical writing) for applicants with a master's degree in or related to computer science; 310 (quantitative + verbal), 4.0 (analytical writing) for applicants with a bachelor's degree in computer science. In addition, the GRE quantitative score must be at least 70th percentile

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Design
Requirements: Applicants must have a graduate degree with a minimum of 32 credit hours and are required to submit three letters of recommendation, a portfolio, statement of interest, and a resume or curriculum vitae. There is no minimum work experience requirement, although two to four years of professional experience is preferred. ID considers full-time internships, volunteer work, and freelance projects as formal work experience. TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for any applicant with an undergraduate degree from an institution where the primary language of instruction is not English. A GRE or GMAT score is also required. [53]
Description: The first PhD in design program in the US, Institute of Design's PhD is a top-rated graduate program for those seeking to teach or conduct fundamental research in the field. Our PhD alumni have gone on to lead noted design programs at universities all over the world and lead practices at global corporations. By pursuing rigorous research in an area that aligns with work by our PhD faculty, you'll work directly in some of the most exciting design-focused work being done today. All PhD students will work closely with their advisors to plan their course of study and research. Students complete a total of 92 credit hours. Up to 32 credits can be transferred from a master's program. Courses might include 12 course credits and 48 research credits. The dissertation created from this work is intended to create a substantial and original contribution to design knowledge.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering
Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree conferred with a minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution for regular admission. [37] Doctoral minimum GRE composite score requirements are 298 (quantitative + verbal) and 3.0 (analytical writing). [36] Letters of recommendation are required for doctoral applicants. [36] The application also requires official transcripts for all post-secondary coursework and a Resume/CV. [36]
ScholarshipAmount: Generally, Ph.D. students are supported with initial monthly stipends of $2,100 or higher.
ScholarshipType: A graduate tuition fellowship and other competitive fellowships may also be awarded.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Finance
Requirements: Admission requirements for the Ph.D. in Finance program include a completed online application and official transcript submission showing a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. [19] GMAT or GRE scores are required. [19] Applicants must also submit a one-page statement of purpose detailing their goals and objectives, along with three to four letters of recommendation from professors or employers. [19] The program requires the successful completion of at least 72 credit hours. [19] Please note that no new students will be accepted into the program for the fall 2026 semester; the next anticipated entry date is the fall 2027 semester. [19]
Description: The Ph.D. in Finance program offers comprehensive coverage of applied statistics, business finance, financial economics, and quantitative finance applied to academic and applied problems in corporate finance, investing, and risk management. [3] The program prepares students to employ tools from these areas to any business problem. [3] The program is research-oriented and prepares graduates capable of initiating advanced research to solve problems in corporate finance, investments, regulatory issues in risk and market functions, and academic roles in finance. [3] Graduates move into successful roles as quantitative research analysts at major investment firms, risk managers for world-class financial institutions, and faculty positions at Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) accredited institutions. [3]
Accredidation: Stuart School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business International. [4, 8]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Food Science and Nutrition
Requirements: An applicant to the doctoral program must hold a master of science degree in microbiology; chemistry; biology; food science; nutrition; chemical, agricultural, food, or environmental engineering; or a related field. The applicant should meet all entrance requirements of the university's Graduate College, plus minimum cumulative undergraduate and graduate GPAs of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale; a GRE score of at least 304 (combined quantitative and verbal); and a minimum English proficiency testing score as follows: TOEFL: 80. IELTS: 6.5. [2]
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Food Science and Nutrition is awarded in recognition of mastery in food science and nutrition and upon demonstration of an ability to make substantial creative contributions to knowledge in food safety, food science, and nutrition. [4, 7] The recipients of the doctoral degree will be capable of continuing independent efforts toward advancement of scientific knowledge in the food-related business. [4, 7] A unique collaborative research program between Illinois Tech and the United States Food and Drug Administration—located on Illinois Tech's Moffett Campus—provides Ph.D. students with the opportunity for focused research interaction with FDA scientists as they pursue their degree. [3, 5]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Industrial-Organizational Psychology
Description: Through a focus on research methods and experience in work settings, the doctoral program in industrial-organizational psychology prepares students for careers in university teaching, industry, government, or consulting. Students will acquire a strong theoretical and methodological background in various areas of industrial-organizational psychology, as well as experience in work settings. Many students have presented and published their work.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Information Technology
Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. program is competitive and applicants must have high grade point averages, GRE scores, and (if required) TOEFL scores. [5]
Description: The doctoral program is designed a student for an academic or industrial research career. To be awarded a Ph.D. in Information Technology, a student must demonstrate mastery in several areas of information technology and must make a significant original contribution to research in the field of information technology. On entry into the program, a student is required to take coursework in a number of areas and pass written and oral qualifying exams. Next, the student must formulate a thesis research problem and present it and the proposed research to a committee of faculty at a comprehensive exam. Upon passing this examination, the student must carry out the research and write and defend a thesis, among other requirements.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Management Science and Analytics
Requirements: Applicants to the Ph.D. in Management Science and Analytics submit comprehensive credentials for the undergraduate and/or graduate degree(s) already completed, an essay outlining the fit between the applicant's background, expertise, and career goals, a detailed resume describing academic/work experience, and letters of recommendation. [1] Applicants to the Ph.D. in Management Science and Analytics program must have completed a master's degree with a graduate level business core, or a master's in finance or equivalent degree. [2] For applicants who have a master's degree but have not completed the business core, some prerequisite courses will be required. [2]
Fees: Estimated $133,272 for the entire program (72 credit hours * $1,851/credit hour).
Fees.1: $1,851 per credit hour for the 2025-2026 academic year. [109]
Description: The Ph.D. in Management Science and Analytics program prepares graduates to identify pressing business community issues, structure problems, gather data, and create innovative, impactful analyses and solutions. Emphasizing analysis and synthesis, the program delivers a comprehensive, advanced education in applying analytical tools, computer models, and quantitative methods to complex decision-making in business, finance, and other disciplines. Graduates move into successful roles as quantitative research analysts at major corporations and faculty positions at Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) accredited institutions. The program prepares students and working professionals for academic careers and executive and management positions in business, government, and consulting. The Ph.D. program emphasizes both analysis and synthesis. The required courses provide the tools to analyze business problems and develop new systems or novel solutions. Once students master these skills, their dissertation work involves structuring a problem, gathering data where appropriate, and solving it. Management science and analytics methodologies can be applied to any aspect of business. The program's goal is to facilitate the contribution of new knowledge to the field of business through applied research that addresses important problems in operations and finance.
Accredidation: The Stuart School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: Doctoral candidates should meet the requirements for a master's degree or present evidence that they have reached an equivalent level of proficiency. A minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution is required for regular admission. [36] In order to be admitted to the program, each student must also be accepted by a thesis adviser and pass a qualifying exam given by the department. [5]
Description: The Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering program prepares individuals to perform original, cutting-edge research in areas including nanostructured materials, advanced semiconductor materials, electronic, optical and magnetic materials, biomimetic materials, polymeric materials, MEMS (micro-electromechanical systems) materials and systems, organic electronics, theory and simulation of materials systems, and advanced processing of modern materials. The Ph.D. program prepares students for professional and research careers in industry, government or academia. Students develop the expertise to make independent contributions to research and development, formulate novel problems, develop creative solutions to novel and existing problems, and serve as system architects and leaders of design teams. Students successful in this program have come from undergraduate and/or M.S.-level study in the areas of materials science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, chemistry and physics. The curriculum ensures that students develop a broad knowledge of modern materials science; that they apply their knowledge and analytical skills to create effective and novel solutions to practical problems; and that they communicate well in professional forums and publications; and that they work effectively in both collaborative and independent settings.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Applicants for the Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering must be accepted by a thesis adviser and pass a qualifying examination given by the department in order to be admitted to candidacy for the doctoral degree. The exam evaluates the student's background in order to determine the student's potential for achieving a doctorate.
Department: Department of Mechanical, Materials, and Aerospace Engineering
Description: This program provides advanced, research-based education and knowledge through advanced coursework, state-of-the-art and original research, and publication of novel results in preparation for careers in academia and industrial research and development. The doctoral degree is awarded in recognition of a high level of mastery in one of the several fields of the department including a significant original research contribution. A student working toward the Ph.D. degree has great flexibility in formulating an overall program to meet individual needs under the guidance of an adviser and the department.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics
Requirements: Illinois Tech requires a four-year bachelor's degree conferred with a minimum cumulative undergraduate grade-point average of 3.0/4.0 (or its equivalent) from an accredited institution for regular admission. [4] Applicants to the doctoral program in physics are expected to have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a major in that same discipline, or a closely allied major. [3] The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is required for all applicants, with a minimum score of 310 (quantitative + verbal) and 3.0 (analytical writing) for Ph.D. applicants. [3, 8] Applicants to the doctoral program in physics are also strongly encouraged, but not required, to take the subject-area GRE exam in physics. [3] The requirements for the degree consist of a program of 72 credit hours, passing the Ph.D. qualifying and comprehensive examinations, and the completion of a research thesis. [5]
Department: Lewis College of Science and Letters
Description: The Ph.D. in physics is a research-based degree. The program is designed to provide a student with advanced knowledge and experience in the field, which will allow them to pursue a career as a professional physicist in academia, industry, or at a government research center. In addition to coursework, a student's progress is evaluated through a qualifying examination, a research-based proposal, and a final thesis defense. Students will select a research adviser and topic of interest early in their studies, and will become a member of a research group working at the forefront of the field. Students may pursue research in a variety of areas in experimental and theoretical physics, including accelerator and particle physics, astrophysics, condensed matter and materials physics, and medical physics/biophysics.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology
Requirements:
Requirements for admission to the program include:
- Bachelor's degree with 18 hours of undergraduate psychology, including successful coursework in research methods or statistics.
- Completed online application, including payment of application fee.
- Professional statement of 1,000 words or fewer outlining academic and career goals, academic potential, and relevant research and/or applied experience.
- Three (3) letters of recommendation, which referees will upload directly into the application system.
- Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions; transcripts must be uploaded directly into the application system.
- A curriculum vitae (CV)
Description: With a recent 10-year re-accreditation decision from the American Psychological Association, Illinois Tech's Ph.D. a clinical psychology offers intensive training based on the Boulder Scientist/Practitioner model and cognitive-behavioral theoretical foundations. [3] The program emphasizes a balance of clinical practice and the understanding and conduct of clinical psychological research, generally preparing you for licensure eligibility (although licensing requirements vary by jurisdiction). [3] Practice experiences include exposure to diverse populations. [3] A student's training in practice and research begins in the first year and continues throughout their graduate career. [3] Illinois Tech trains students from the cognitive-behavioral framework to be scientist-practitioners. [3] You'll learn the scientific process of psychological research, and receive extensive clinical training to prepare you to become a clinical psychologist and thought leader in the field. [3]
Accredidation: Illinois Tech's Ph.D. in clinical psychology has been fully accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA) since 1982. [3, 4]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Rehabilitation Counseling Education
Requirements: Minimum requirements for admission include a Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling, preferably, with at least one year of post-master's work experience recommended, a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0, a minimum graduate GPA of 3.5, minimum GRE scores of verbal 151 and quantitative 153 (taken in the past five years), three letters of recommendation, a professional statement, transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, and a personal interview. [5]
Department: Lewis College of Science and Letters, Department of Psychology
Description: The Rehabilitation Counseling Education PhD program is designed to train doctoral-level students to become professional counselor educators who are proficient in advanced-level counseling, post-secondary teaching, clinical supervision, research, scholarship, leadership, and advocacy. [1] This program offers a student-focused and research-based curriculum that prepares leaders in the field of rehabilitation counseling at the highest level. [1, 2] Faculty at the Illinois Institute of Technology view rehabilitation counseling as a specialized area of professional counseling where the main goal is to help individuals with a disability or chronic illness achieve psychological and economic independence. [1] The program of study includes the equivalent of two years of full-time coursework and supervised experience, in addition to dissertation research. [1] Students typically enter the program with a 60-credit-hour master's degree in rehabilitation counseling or a related field. [1] The curriculum consists of 54 credit hours of coursework, with the potential to transfer 15 credits from a qualifying master's degree, plus 24 credit hours for the dissertation. [1] Students are required to pass an oral qualifying exam and a written comprehensive exam before starting their dissertation research. [1]
Accredidation: The Rehabilitation Counseling Education PhD program is fully accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Programs (CACREP) in the area of Counselor Education and Supervision. [1, 2]
ScholarshipType: Teaching assistantships, funding support through research projects, and adjunct course instructor positions are available for doctoral students. [71]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Technology and Humanities
Requirements: Students enter the Ph. D. program from a wide range of fields but should have substantial academic preparation or professional experience related to one or more humanities fields. Applicants must have completed a bachelor's or master's degree in a field that, in combination with the 30 credit hour technical core, would provide a solid basis for advanced academic work leading to original research in technology and humanities.
Description: The Dissertation should constitute an original contribution to scholarship in technology and humanities and may address areas of interaction between technology and humanities and other disciplines (e.g., history, linguistics, literature, philosophy, and rhetoric/ composition). [6] The research topic and method may be empirical (perhaps employing the facilities of the Humanities and Technology Lab or Speech Analysis Lab), pedagogical, historical, or theoretical. [4, 6] The Ph.D. in technology and humanities prepares students for faculty-line and alternative academic careers in university research and teaching, as well as for advanced research and development positions in the private and government sectors. [7] You will establish a strong foundation in the digital research methods necessary to deeply investigate the unique problems surrounding humans and their relationships to technology. [7] Additionally, you'll learn to consider technology through the theoretical lenses of a number of core humanities disciplines, such as history, language, media studies, communication, and philosophy. [7]
Accredidation: Illinois Institute of Technology is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (hlcommission.org). [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Illinois Tech is a member of the Common Application. First-year applicants can apply by submitting the Common Application online. There is no application fee to apply to Illinois Tech. Applicants must also submit an official high school transcript.
ProgramWebsiteURL:
The official university website for the Illinois Institute of Technology is www.iit.edu.

Illinois Tech, as it is commonly known, is a private research university located in Chicago. The university offers a wide range of programs in fields such as architecture, business, communications, design, engineering, and science.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $15,000 annually for the SPARC Scholarship. [53]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Behavioral Health and Wellness
Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed application and official transcripts from all high schools attended. [2, 5] The university conducts a holistic application review that considers high school performance (including course selection and rigor), essays/personal statement, and choice of major. [3] Students may choose to submit letters of recommendation and standardized test scores, but these are not required. [5]
Department: Lewis College of Science and Letters
Description: The behavioral health and wellness degree is interdisciplinary, and combines coursework in psychology, sociology, political science, and nutritional science. You can also customize your program with an elective specialty track in either health psychology, public health, or nutrition. A capstone project will help you integrate and apply the concepts and skills you learned to a real-life situation, preparing you to make an impact your first day on the job. [2] As a student in the Bachelor of Science in Behavioral Health and Wellness program in the Lewis College of Human Sciences, you will develop your understanding of how lifestyle choices impact health over time, and how to design individualized programs to promote healthy living, most often related to nutrition, exercise, and tobacco and alcohol use. [2] You'll also become a patient advocate, educating patients on how to steer through the daunting bureaucracy of health care services. [2] The behavioral health and wellness degree program will provide students with a broad understanding of how lifestyle choices impact health, and how health professionals design programs to promote healthy lifestyle choices. [3] Students will develop an understanding of three core areas: Intervention development and implementation, Community care coordination, and Public health policy. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychological Science
Requirements: For undergraduate admission, applicants must submit a completed application, transcripts from all high schools attended, and transcripts of all colleges where applicable. [3] For graduate admission, a four-year bachelor's degree with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is generally required, along with official transcripts, a professional statement, letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV. [8, 12] International students must also submit proof of English proficiency. [4]
Department: Lewis College of Science and Letters
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior—how individuals think, feel, and behave. Graduates will have a strong background in scientific thinking and be able to apply psychological research and principles to the study of contemporary problems in a variety of fields. Students in the psychological science aprogram will develop an understanding of: How people perceive and process information and how they use that information to make decisions; Psychological theories in a variety of fields including social, cognitive, clinical, industrial-organizational, development, and neuroscience; How to apply psychological theories to real-world problems; How to design research studies, analyze results, and communicate results to different audiences. [10] A flexible curriculum allows the degree to be customized according to interests. [10] Students will work with a faculty mentor to craft a program of study that supports their interests and career goals. Options for pre-medicine and honors law are available. [10] The psychological science degree will prepare graduates for a wide range of professions in business and industry, community organizations, and health services. The program will also prepare graduates to be competitive for a wide range of graduate training programs in psychology at the masters and doctoral levels. [10]
